waves: r12-recover-rejected (needs both: it reuses the parser from clean and the validation semantics from touch/scope)

tasks.title: Make `af validate` reject a declared `touch` entry that no `scope` entry covers (validate_rejects_a_touch_entry_the_scope_does_not_cover)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn validate_rejects_a_touch_entry_the_scope_does_not_cover' tests/contract_config.rs && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: turn the most expensive recurring mistake in this project into a config-time error.

Three campaigns in a row (rounds 8, 10, 11) shipped a task that was UNPASSABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: the operator believed a file was editable while the task's `scope` did not allow it. The agent was then failed for doing the required work, the attempt's spend (~1800-2200s each time) became waste, and the only recovery was to kill the campaign, widen the scope by hand and re-run. In round 11 the operator's own prose for the task named `src/router.rs` while the scope array omitted it.

FIX: a new OPTIONAL task field `touch: Vec<String>` — the files the operator BELIEVES the agent must edit. `config::load` validation SHALL REJECT the config (an `Err`, so `af validate` exits 2 — NOT a warning) when a declared `touch` entry is covered by no `scope` entry, because that task cannot succeed: it must edit a file its own scope forbids. Fail fast, before any agent is paid.

EXACT REQUIREMENTS
1. `Task.touch: Vec<String>` in `src/config.rs`, with `#[serde(default)]`. `Task` already derives `Default` and EVERY literal construction site in the tree uses `..Default::default()`, so this field needs no other file to change — do NOT edit anything outside your scope.
2. Put the check inside `fn validate(tasks: &[Task], workers: &[Worker]) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>` in `src/config.rs`, which already returns `Err` for fatal config problems and `Ok(warnings)` otherwise. Visit tasks in file order and their `touch` entries in declaration order.
3. Coverage MUST be decided by the SAME matcher the enforcement path uses: `crate::scheduler::scope_overlap(path, scope_entry)` (a `pub fn` in `src/scheduler.rs`, out of your scope — call it, do not re-implement it). `src/execute.rs::scope_violations` documents itself as using "the SAME matcher as the scheduler ... so admission control and enforcement agree on what 'in scope' means", and that property is the entire point of this check: it must be impossible for validation to accept a config that enforcement will later reject. Do not write a second glob implementation.
4. An EMPTY `scope` means "any file" (existing semantics, see `scope_violations`): then every `touch` entry is covered and nothing is ever rejected.
5. An empty or absent `touch` is the normal case (all 51 existing campaign tasks declare none): never warn, never error, no output change at all for them.
6. Error text: name the task, the offending entry, and the scope, deterministically — `task '<id>': touch entry '<path>' is covered by no scope entry (<scope entries joined with ", ">)`. No timestamps, no absolute paths. The message must make the fix obvious (widen `scope` or drop the entry).
7. Do NOT add any other new warning or error. A `touch` entry naming a file that does not exist yet is FINE (the task may create it) — no existence checks.
8. Tests in `tests/contract_config.rs`, driven through the public loader the way the neighbouring tests are: the REQUIRED test is `validate_rejects_a_touch_entry_the_scope_does_not_cover` — write it FIRST, run it, and confirm it fails for the right reason (the config loads today instead of being rejected) before implementing. It must assert a rejection naming the task id and the path. Also cover: the covered arm (a `touch` entry matching an exact path, matching a directory prefix, and matching a glob — all accepted), the empty-`touch` arm, the empty-`scope` arm (everything covered), and that the error is an `Err` (never a panic).
9. Document the new field and the rule in `openspec/specs/config/spec.md`: add `touch` to the schema sentence listing the supported task fields and add a scenario for the rejection. Every existing scenario must stay intact — a modified requirement is a REPLACEMENT, so reproduce the surviving text verbatim.
10. Run the repo's own CI checks before you stop (`openspec validate --specs`, `./scripts/coverage-gate.sh`, `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`); the acceptance gate runs exactly those.

tasks.title: Make `af clean` prune archived `<prefix>/<id>-rejected-*` branches while keeping those of running tasks (clean_removes_archived_rejected_branches)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn clean_removes_archived_rejected_branches' tests/contract_worktree.rs && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: sweep the refs that round 11's archiving leaves behind.

Round 11 made a failed attempt's committed work recoverable: on a scope violation or a merge conflict the attempt branch is COPIED to `<prefix>/<id>-rejected-<unix-ts>` before cleanup (`worktree::archive_branch`, `src/worktree.rs`) and the receipt names it. Nothing ever removes those refs. Every recovered failure therefore leaves one behind forever, and the operator's only recourse is manual `git branch -D`. `af clean [--dry-run]` already sweeps worktrees and branches left by crashed runs — extend it to sweep these too.

EXACT REQUIREMENTS
1. Task ids contain hyphens (`r11-measured-cost`) and round 11 appends a `-<n>` suffix when the first choice of name is taken, so the archived name is always `<prefix>/<id>-rejected-<ts>` or `<prefix>/<id>-rejected-<ts>-<n>`. Write a PURE, unit-testable helper in `src/worktree.rs` that recovers the task id from such a branch name (for example `tf/r11-measured-cost-rejected-1791259017` -> `r11-measured-cost`, `tf/x-rejected-1-2` -> `x`), returning `None` for a branch that is not an archived rejected branch of this prefix (`tf/x`, `other/x-rejected-1`). Unit-test it directly; get the hyphen and suffix handling right rather than guessing with a substring search.
2. Add the sweep to the `af clean` path: `worktree::clean` (`src/worktree.rs`) and/or `pub fn clean` (`src/run.rs`), whichever keeps the code honest — but the CLI contract below is fixed.
3. CLI contract:
   - `af clean --dry-run` prints `would remove branch <name>` for every archived branch that WOULD be removed and touches nothing (no git mutation whatsoever).
   - `af clean` prints `removed branch <name>` for each and actually removes it (`git branch --list` no longer shows it).
   - An archived branch whose task is still marked RUNNING in the state file MUST be kept, exactly like the running-worktree rule — and must not be reported as removed.
   - The existing orphan-worktree behaviour, ordering and messages stay byte-identical.
   - IMPORTANT: `run::clean` currently returns early with `clean: no orphaned worktrees under <root>` when there are no orphan worktrees. That short-circuit must not skip the branch sweep — a repo with archived branches and no orphan worktrees still has work to do. When there is genuinely nothing to do, the existing message stays byte-identical.
   - Exit code stays 0; a git error is never fatal (the sweep is best-effort, like `archive_branch` itself).
4. Do NOT change `archive_branch`'s naming contract — round 11's receipts point at those names.
5. Tests: the REQUIRED test is `clean_removes_archived_rejected_branches` in `tests/contract_worktree.rs` — write it FIRST, run it, and confirm it fails for the right reason (the branches survive today) before implementing. Cover: the sweep removes them; a running task's archived branch survives; `dry_run = true` reports and removes nothing; the parser handles the `-<n>` collision form and ignores a foreign prefix and a non-rejected branch. Add a CLI-level arm in `tests/cli.rs` for the user-visible `--dry-run` output and the keep-if-running rule, following that file's existing scratch-repo/`Cli` conventions.
6. Document it in `openspec/specs/worktree/spec.md`: extend the `af clean` requirement and add a scenario. Keep every surviving scenario verbatim (a modified requirement REPLACES the old block, so reproduce the text you keep).
7. Run the repo's own CI checks before you stop (`openspec validate --specs`, `./scripts/coverage-gate.sh`, `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`); the acceptance gate runs exactly those.

tasks.title: Add `af recover --task ID` to re-validate an archived rejected branch and merge it without re-running the agent (recover_merges_an_archived_branch_after_revalidating_scope_and_gate)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn recover_merges_an_archived_branch' tests/cli.rs && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: make the paid-for work that round 11 preserves actually usable, so the operator never re-buys it.

Round 11 archives a failed attempt's branch as `<branch>-rejected-<ts>` (see `worktree::archive_branch` in `src/worktree.rs`). The most valuable case is a SCOPE VIOLATION caused by an over-narrow scope — the operator's error, measured at 2200.7s (round 8), 1987.4s (round 10) and 1785.8s (round 11). In those cases the agent's committed work was CORRECT and complete; it had merely touched one extra file that the scope should have allowed. Today the only recovery is to kill the campaign, widen the scope, and re-run the agent from scratch, re-buying work already paid for. `af recover` closes that loop: re-validate the archived branch against the CURRENT scope and gate, and merge it if it passes — never re-invoking the agent.

EXACT REQUIREMENTS
1. New subcommand `af recover --task ID [--dry-run]`. Parse it in `src/main.rs`'s `parse` mirroring the `clean` arm; `Args` already carries `task` and `dry_run`, so no new field, and wire it to `pub fn recover(cfg: &Config, st: &Settings, id: &str, dry_run: bool) -> i32` in `src/run.rs`.
2. SELECTION. Look in the task's repo (`cfg.repo_dir_for`) for branches matching `<branch_prefix>/<id>-rejected-<ts>` (and the round-11 collision form `...-rejected-<ts>-<n>`) and pick the NEWEST. Newest MUST be decided by PARSING the numeric `<ts>` (then `<n>`) — never by git's output order and never by committer dates: the same branch set must always select the same branch. `src/worktree.rs` already gains a pure parser for these names in this round (`r12-clean-rejected`); reuse or mirror it rather than writing a second parser.
3. EXIT CODES AND MESSAGES. Unknown task -> exit 2 (`config error: unknown task '<id>'`). No archived branch -> exit 2 with a message naming the pattern searched (nothing to recover is not a failure). The re-validation failing -> exit 1, leaving the archived branch in place. Success -> exit 0.
4. RE-VALIDATION, in this order, before any merge:
   a. SCOPE: the paths the archived branch changes relative to the merge base with the base branch must ALL be covered by the task's CURRENT `scope` (that is the whole point: the operator widened it). Reuse the enforcement helpers — `changed_paths` and `scope_violations` in `src/execute.rs` (hoist their visibility if needed) — and call `crate::scheduler::scope_overlap` through them rather than reimplementing globs. An empty scope means any file. If anything is still out of scope, print the violation the way the attempt path does and exit 1.
   b. GATE: unless `task.manual`, check the archived branch out in a worktree and run the acceptance gate with `gate::run_accept`, exactly as `src/execute.rs` does (including the task's `gate_replay`). A non-zero gate -> print the failure and exit 1. The temporary worktree must be removed on EVERY exit path, so a failed recover leaves no worktree behind (see `worktree::remove` / the existing `cleanup` helper in `src/execute.rs`).
   c. `--dry-run`: perform the selection and print exactly what it would do, then exit 0 WITHOUT touching anything — no worktree, no gate run, no merge.
5. SUCCESS PATH: merge the archived branch into the base with `worktree::merge` and the standard merge message `af: <id> — <title>` (the same one `finish_resume_merge` in `src/run.rs` uses); set the task's state to `Done` with `phase = GatePassed` and persist it (the same shape `finish_resume_merge` writes); remove the recovered worktree and the archived branch (its content is now in the base — leaving it behind would be a ghost for `af clean`); print `✓ <id> recovered to done (agent not re-run)`.
6. HISTORY IS APPEND-ONLY. The failed attempt's receipt stays exactly as it is: the ledger honestly records the attempt that failed, and `af cost` keeps reporting it. Do not rewrite or delete receipts. `af` never pushes, and recovery never re-invokes the agent.
7. Tests: the REQUIRED test is `recover_merges_an_archived_branch_after_revalidating_scope_and_gate` in `tests/cli.rs` — write it FIRST, run it, and confirm it fails for the right reason (`af recover` is not a subcommand today) before implementing. It must be an end-to-end CLI test in a scratch git repo: create an archived `tf/<id>-rejected-<ts>` branch carrying a commit that is in scope and passes the gate, run `af recover --task <id>`, and assert exit 0, the task is `Done` in the state file, the change is in the base branch, and the archived branch is gone. Add the negative arms as tests too: an out-of-scope branch -> exit 1 and the branch survives; a gate-failing branch -> exit 1; `--dry-run` -> exit 0 with nothing changed; unknown task and no-archived-branch -> exit 2. Unit-test the branch selection (newest wins, the `-<n>` collision form, a foreign prefix ignored) in the appropriate file.
8. SPEC: document the subcommand and its exit codes in `openspec/specs/cli/spec.md`, and the archived-branch lifecycle in `openspec/specs/worktree/spec.md` if that is where round 11's archiving is described. Keep every surviving scenario verbatim (a modified requirement REPLACES the old block).
9. Run the repo's own CI checks before you stop (`openspec validate --specs`, `./scripts/coverage-gate.sh`, `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`); the acceptance gate runs exactly those.
